subject: Get the p-value for all SNPs in QTL calculation

messages.author: d8f0f3c1907e0b89
messages.subject: Get the p-value for all SNPs in QTL calculation
parts:
Hi all,

I was just using r/qtl to calculate the p-values of the QTLs in my study, but scanone will only give me the lod scores of each SNP, and summary will only give me the peak p-value of each chromosome. Do you have some ideas/suggestions to get the p-values for all SNPs when I'm using r/qtl?

Thank you.

Hao

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Get the p-value for all SNPs in QTL calculation
parts:
The p-value is the proportion of permutations with LOD score greater than or equal to the observed LOD, so you could go through the LODs for each SNP and calculate those proportions.

# example analysis and permutations
data(fake.bc)
fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=2.5)
out <- scanone(fake.bc, method="hk")
operm <- scanone(fake.bc, method="hk", n.perm=1000)

# calculate p-values
pval <- sapply(out[,3], function(a,b) mean(b >= a), operm)

# the same thing, via a for loop
pval <- rep(NA, nrow(out))
for(i in 1:nrow(out))
pval[i] <- mean(operm >= out[i,3])

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Get the p-value for all SNPs in QTL calculation
parts:
The p-values are the proportion of permutation replicates that are >= the observed LOD score.
So if you do 1000 replicates, the p-value will come out as a fraction x/1000 and so something like 0.043.

karl
